text: In group epistemology, the deflationary view that a group believes p if and only if a sufficient proportion of its members individually believe p, so that group belief is nothing more than the aggregate of individual beliefs, is called ___.
explanation: Summativism is the deflationary thesis that group belief just is a suitable function of the beliefs of individual members, adding no new ontology. Its rival, non-summativism (Gilbert, Pettit), holds that group belief is a distinct phenomenon of joint commitment or acceptance not reducible to members' beliefs. The discursive dilemma is standardly deployed against simple summative aggregation.
